material_systems.name: PVA Drywall Ceiling Primer
material_systems.description: Polyvinyl acetate (PVA) primer for bare drywall ceilings. Economical drywall sealer — seals porosity and provides base for topcoat. Zero stain blocking capability.

example_products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec PVA Primer
products.notes: PVA primer is a drywall sealer ONLY. It seals porous drywall and provides holdout for topcoats. It has ZERO stain blocking capability — do not confuse with stain-blocking primers, which are an entirely separate product category. Water cleanup.

material_systems.name: Acrylic Latex Drywall Ceiling Primer
material_systems.description: Premium acrylic latex primer for bare drywall ceilings. Superior adhesion and topcoat holdout compared to PVA. Zero stain blocking capability.

example_products: Benjamin Moore Fresh Start Premium Interior Primer
PPG Speedhide Interior Acrylic Latex Primer
products.notes: Acrylic latex provides better adhesion and topcoat holdout than PVA. Does NOT provide stain blocking — that is a separate product category. Water cleanup.

material_systems.name: High-Build Drywall Ceiling Primer
material_systems.description: High-build primer for ceilings requiring Level 5 finish or maximum surface uniformity. Fills minor imperfections and provides uniform porosity. Zero stain blocking capability.

example_products: Benjamin Moore Ultra Spec High Build Interior Primer
products.notes: High-build formula fills minor imperfections and provides uniform porosity across joints and field. May require light sanding after application. Does NOT provide stain blocking. Water cleanup.

coverage_profiles.assumptions: Bare drywall ceiling, proper application thickness, standard porosity. Ceiling application may consume slightly more material than walls due to overhead drip.
Level 3 has more exposed paper, higher absorption, lower coverage
Texture increases surface area, reduces coverage 15-25%
Premium primer on bare drywall ceiling
High-build applied at greater thickness, lower coverage by design. Ceiling application may further reduce coverage slightly.

consumables.name: 18-inch roller cover, 3/8" to 1/2" nap
consumables.specification: 18-inch production roller cover, 3/8 to 1/2 inch nap, synthetic blend
consumables.notes: 18" is standard for ceiling production. Nap selection is contractor's discretion: 3/8" for reduced stipple, 1/2" for standard coverage. Both are appropriate for smooth drywall.

consumables.name: 18-inch roller cover, 1/2" to 3/4" nap
consumables.specification: 18-inch production roller cover, 1/2 to 3/4 inch nap, synthetic blend
consumables.notes: Orange peel and knockdown are light textures — 1/2" nap is often sufficient. 3/4" nap only needed for heavier textures (popcorn, stomp finish) which are uncommon on new construction ceilings.

consumables.name: 18-inch roller frame
consumables.specification: 18-inch production roller frame with threaded handle
consumables.notes: Production roller frame for overhead ceiling work

consumables.name: Extension pole
consumables.notes: Required for overhead ceiling work at standard heights

consumables.name: 5-gallon bucket with grid
consumables.notes: Standard for production ceiling work. 5-gallon containers preferred for production.

consumables.name: Spray tip 517
consumables.notes: 517 tip standard for drywall primer — good coverage and manageable fan width for ceiling work.

consumables.name: Spray gun filter
consumables.specification: In-line filter for airless spray gun
consumables.notes: Replace when clogged or every ~50 gallons

consumables.name: Plastic sheeting (lightweight)
consumables.specification: 0.5-1 mil plastic sheeting for lightweight overspray protection
consumables.notes: Lightweight plastic for pinning over window/door openings to prevent overspray fallout. Not intricate masking — just catch the fallout. At this NC phase, typically only exterior doors installed.

consumables.name: Masking tape 1.5-inch
consumables.notes: For tacking plastic over openings and general masking. 60 yards = 180 LF per roll. All tape rolls are 60 yards (180 LF) regardless of width.

consumables.name: Masking paper 12-inch
consumables.notes: For stuffing recessed lights, ceiling electrical boxes, and open ceiling holes during spray. 180 LF per roll — all masking paper rolls are 180 LF regardless of width.

consumables.name: Rosin paper (floor protection — hard surfaces)
consumables.specification: Red rosin paper, 36-inch width, taped seams
consumables.notes: DEFAULT floor protection for ceiling spray over finished hard floors. Full coverage, taped down at edges and seams. No risk of overspray reaching finished flooring. 500 SF per roll.

consumables.name: Masking tape for rosin paper edges/seams
consumables.specification: 2-inch painter's tape or masking tape for taping rosin paper edges and seams
consumables.notes: Tape down rosin paper edges and seams to prevent movement and overspray infiltration.

consumables.name: Drop cloth / plastic sheeting (floor protection — carpet)
consumables.specification: Canvas drop cloths or plastic sheeting for carpeted floor protection
consumables.notes: CONDITIONAL — for carpeted areas only. Canvas drop cloths or plastic sheeting appropriate for carpet. Canvas 4x12 = 48 SF per cloth.

consumables.name: Sandpaper 220 grit (pole sander)
consumables.specification: 220 grit sandpaper sheets for pole sander
consumables.notes: Sanding primed surface before finish coat is a finish task step (belongs in SF_DRYWALL_CEILINGS_NC_PAINT scope, not prime scope). Included here only as reference for high-build primer situations where sanding may be needed before the surface is ready for the finish spec to take over.

consumable_usage_models.description: Ceiling opening/fixture protection — stuff or cover recessed can holes, electrical box holes, and any installed fixtures with paper. In NC, many ceiling openings will be open holes where recessed cans and electrical boxes have NOT yet been installed. These still must be filled to prevent overspray entry and to keep blown-in/blown-out insulation from coming through during spraying.
consumable_usage_models.heuristic: 6 recessed light locations + 2 ceiling electrical box locations per room average. These may be installed fixtures OR open holes awaiting installation.

consumable_usage_models.description: Lightweight plastic over window openings — pin to prevent overspray fallout
consumable_usage_models.notes: Lightweight protection — pin plastic over opening. Not intricate masking.

consumable_usage_models.description: Lightweight plastic over door openings — pin to prevent overspray fallout. At this NC phase, typically exterior doors only.
consumable_usage_models.notes: Lightweight protection — pin plastic over opening. Typically only exterior doors at this phase (interior doors usually not installed yet).

consumable_usage_models.description: Full rosin paper floor protection for finished hard floors — taped down at edges and seams. Default for ceiling spray over finished flooring.
consumable_usage_models.notes: Full floor coverage with rosin paper, taped seams. No risk tolerance for overspray on finished hard floors.

consumable_usage_models.description: Canvas/plastic floor protection for carpeted areas — CONDITIONAL on floor_type=finished, floor_surface=carpet
consumable_usage_models.notes: Canvas drop cloths or plastic sheeting for carpeted areas.

compatibility_rules.description: PVA primer is compatible with all latex/acrylic topcoats
compatibility_rules.constraint: Do not apply solvent-based topcoats over PVA primer

compatibility_rules.description: High-build primer may require sanding before topcoat
compatibility_rules.constraint: Light sand with 220 grit after high-build application, before finish coat

compatibility_rules.description: Match primer manufacturer to planned topcoat manufacturer when possible
compatibility_rules.constraint: Preferred, not required. Manufacturer systems are optimized for intercoat adhesion.

risk_notes.description: Overhead ceiling application consumes slightly more material due to drip and sag compared to wall application
risk_notes.mitigation: Use conservative coverage rates (low end of range) for ceiling estimating

risk_notes.description: Level 3 drywall has higher porosity and may consume 15%+ more primer than Level 4/5
risk_notes.mitigation: Use Level 3 coverage profile; consider second coat if joint pattern telegraphs

risk_notes.description: PVA and acrylic latex drywall primers have ZERO stain blocking capability. If stains are present (water stains, marker, etc.), a dedicated stain-blocking primer is required as a separate product.
risk_notes.mitigation: Do not rely on drywall primer for stain blocking. Specify dedicated stain-blocking primer if needed — that is a separate scope item.

material_quantity_notes.primer_calculation: Ceiling SF × 1 coat ÷ coverage rate = gallons needed
material_quantity_notes.coat_count: Single coat for all quality tiers (QT2-QT5)
material_quantity_notes.consumable_calculation: Driven by application method and room/opening counts
material_quantity_notes.floor_protection_note: Floor protection ONLY when floor_type=finished. Default: rosin paper taped down (full coverage) for hard floors. Canvas/plastic for carpet. Zero floor protection on subfloor.
material_quantity_notes.brand_policy: Use top-tier manufacturer products only: Sherwin-Williams, Benjamin Moore, PPG
